sources.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sources.authors: Shunyu Yao, Noah Shinn, Pedram Razavi, Karthik Narasimhan (Sierra)

cache.timestamp_basis: Downloaded PDF file modification time; browser request timestamp was not separately captured.

sections: §5, pp.6–7: model/method settings and Figure 4 reliability
§5.2 p.7: task ambiguity found on trajectory review
supported_claims: pass@k means at least one success among k iid trials; pass^k means all k successful, averaged across tasks. Both differ from pooling task runs without task identity.
For a task with n observed trials, c successes: unbiased estimators are 1-C(n-c,k)/C(n,k) and C(c,k)/C(n,k), then task average. When n=k, pass^k is the fraction of tasks whose k runs all pass.
Database end-state equality is necessary but not sufficient for policy compliance; user confirmation violations may remain undetected.

numerical_claims.claim: Main task set: 115 retail + 50 airline tasks; main table uses at least 3 trials/task; agent temperature 0, simulated user temperature 1.
numerical_claims.denominator: Task population is synthetic customer service, not code generation. Figure 4 has more repeats than main table; avoid presenting main-table trial count as Figure 4 design.

numerical_claims.claim: GPT-4o function-calling retail pass^1 61.2%; retail pass^8 below25%.
numerical_claims.denominator: 115 retail tasks; Figure4 repeated trials, stochastic user and agent; do not transfer rates to coding.

limits: User simulator adds stochasticity; fixed customer-service scenario is not byte-identical coding packet.
Only one local parser task cannot estimate a population-level pass^k across software tasks.
sources.use: Formal distinction and concrete operational question; old performance numbers optional, not contemporary model ranking.

sources.title: Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals

cache.capture_note: gstack browse goto + text; captured page text, including navigation

supported_claims: CPU/RAM guarantees and kill thresholds change agentic eval results; the harness/runtime is part of treatment conditions.
Binomial sampling intervals do not absorb unmodeled infrastructure differences.
Provider recommends reporting guaranteed allocation plus hard ceiling, calibrated to the benchmark, not universally 3×.

numerical_claims.claim: Terminal-Bench 2.0: six resource settings with the same model, harness, and task set; strict 1× to uncapped improved by 6 percentage points (p < .01).
numerical_claims.denominator: The article does not publish the task or run count for this experiment. Preserve this limitation if using the number.

numerical_claims.claim: SWE-bench crossover: 227 problems with 10 samples each; available RAM increased from 1× to 5×, with a 1.54-percentage-point improvement at 5×.
numerical_claims.denominator: The article does not state whether the 10 samples are per resource condition. Do not infer a total request count.

limits: Vendor internal experiments; no complete open dataset/individual model identity in article.
Local parser generation has no tool runtime, so this does not prove its observed variation came from RAM. It motivates versioned runtime records for future agent-loop studies.
sources.use: Mechanism for why fixed prompt and model name alone do not define a repeatable treatment.

sources.title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
sources.authors: Jiawei Liu, Chunqiu Steven Xia, Yuyao Wang, Lingming Zhang

cache.capture_note: gstack browse goto + text; captured page text, including navigation

supported_claims: More discriminating tests can change correctness verdicts and rankings on the same generated programs; increasing generation repeats cannot repair a blind grader.
Input contracts exclude invalid/undefined inputs from unfair grading and clarify intended domain.
Contracts themselves can be incomplete; ground-truth programs also needed review.

numerical_claims.claim: HumanEval has 164 tasks; the study evaluates 26 models and expands the test suite by approximately 80×.
numerical_claims.denominator: Small Python function synthesis. Most models use 200 samples per task at each temperature (.2, .4, .6, .8), plus greedy decoding. GPT-4 uses greedy decoding only; ChatGPT has limited random sampling. Do not imply identical sampling across all 26 models.

numerical_claims.claim: Maximum relative reductions: 19.3% for pass@1, 24.9% for pass@10, 28.9% for pass@100, and 23.1% for greedy pass@1*.
numerical_claims.denominator: Maxima across evaluated models, not percentage-point changes or average effects. Omit these percentages unless they are needed.

limits: Expanded tests improve bug detection but still do not prove universal correctness.
Localparser R02–R10 deliberately define malformed-input behavior, so invalid JSON shapes cannot be discarded just because EvalPlus filters inputs outside its own contracts.
sources.use: Why test adequacy must be checked before interpreting ten repetitions as reliability; useful contract boundary counterexample.

sources.title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
sources.authors: Joel Becker, Nate Rush, Tom Cunningham, David Rein, Khalid Mahamud (METR)

cache.capture_note: gstack browse goto + text; captured page text, including navigation

sections: Wider adoption of AI has made it more difficult to measure task-level productivity
supported_claims: The investigators consider the update unreliable for estimating the current productivity effect because developer selection, task selection, and attribution of time during concurrent work changed.
Participants may omit tasks they expect AI to help with before randomization. Randomization after selection does not repair representativeness.
Concurrent agent work makes elapsed time and active human work distinct measurements.

numerical_claims.claim: 57 developers: 10 returning and 47 new, across 143 repositories and more than 800 tasks.
numerical_claims.denominator: Recruitment pay changed from USD 150/hour to USD 50/hour. Tasks were randomized to AI-allowed or AI-disallowed. This is not an unbiased sample of all developers or tasks.

numerical_claims.claim: Returning participants: estimate −18%, confidence interval −38% to +9%; new participants: estimate −4%, confidence interval −15% to +9%.
numerical_claims.denominator: The authors describe the estimates as very weak evidence for effect size because of selection. Do not present them as evidence of no speedup or as a current 4% speedup.

limits: The update does not establish long-term maintainability outcomes.
sources.use: Strong why-inconclusive-is-a-decision story; what to record when agentparallelism changes measurement.
